tex_content.html:
Corollary
[constant isotropy type gives a Riemannian quotient]

Source: petersen:page-0227 ↗ cor:pet-ch5-isotropy-near-orbit ↗ thm:pet-ch5-free-slice-theorem 1. ch5:5.6.26If $H\subset \operatorname {Iso}(M,g)$ is closed and all isotropy groups are conjugate, the orbit space is a Riemannian manifold and $M\to H\backslash M$ a Riemannian submersion.
Proof

↗ cor:pet-ch5-conjugate-isotropy-manifold \sketch By subsection 6.4, conjugate isotropy makes all slice models have one stabilizer type. The charts from subsection 6.4 therefore patch as in subsection 6.4; the normal-space metric descends and makes the quotient map a Riemannian submersion.

□
